A USB (Universal Serial Bus) flash drive is a plug-and-play portable storage device that uses flash memory and is small and lightweight, easily able to be attached to a keychain. Flash memory is a kind of memory storage device for computers and electronic devices. Flash memory is a kind of computer chip with no moving parts that retains its data even when powered off. USB flash drives are also commonly known as USB drives, flash drives, USB sticks, USB thumb drives, key drives and pen drives. USB drives are widely used for writing and transferring computer files such as documents, spreadsheets and images. What Are USB Ports? USB ports are the connectors used to attach USB devices to a computer. USB ports come in several shapes and sizes, you can read more here. USB-A ports are usually found on computers and are rectangular in shape, while USB-C ports are found on mobile devices such as phones, tablets, and digital cameras.
